changes: In MATRIX the LEV box is always labelled with the track's destination (MN, PHN, M+C, ...), not only while CUE is held, so each track's routing stays in view. The value shown while turning LEVEL is still the level; XLV (scene editing), FUNC's MAIN view, NORMAL, STUDIO and MIDI tracks are as before. The author tested the label on an MKII from a card image (OMXLBL01, 13-14 Oct 2026) built before the DSP change below.

Smaller core-0 DSP code: 727 code + 42 table words become 657 + 14 (671 in all), with the same output sample for sample in 26 emulator scenarios (ot_emu: every destination, levels moving, MASTER, MKII, DIR, destination changes during playback). Worst case 4,240 -> 4,194 executed instructions per 16-sample frame, 275 per sample with the headphone crossfade. Emulator only: this DSP code has not run on hardware.

USB: the Modwerk base carries Output Matrix's DSP engine, so the smaller engine needs a new base, and the label needs a re-ported controller package (20 stock sites instead of 19, six stock-copy spans). Both are built locally (base 3e3e3de1, package e2df2fbf) and not published; the published base and the 0.1.0 package are unchanged. On the author's MKII over USB (RAM-booted base, 16 Oct 2026) the switch into MATRIX and back, the label, routing to MAIN, CUE, PHONES, a mono jack and OFF, and the PHONES level passed; the first trial's rollback was refused once (needs-recovery) and completed by the base on its own. On the flashed base a power cycle kept MATRIX, the routing and six other modules installed beside it; after it the LEV box showed stock's split bars until CUE redrew the page (display only). Not checked on the unit for this version: project or Part reload and MASTER TRACK.
Test-only: the gate compares runs over the same samples from transport start, which removes a false DIR AB 127 failure in combined images. Gate 117/117 in the emulator.

First release: the CUE CFG box, titled OUT CFG with the module, gains MATRIX, which makes the headphone jack a third assignable output beside MAIN and CUE. CUE + LEVEL picks each track's outputs (any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one of six mono jacks); the routing lives in the Part. MIX becomes the PHONES level, and the metronome also plays on PHONES.
Switching to or from MATRIX converts every Part's LEVEL and cue bytes by documented rules, and switching into NORMAL also sets the project's cue settings.
Builds with the stock DSP code built in: its core-0 code takes a given-up stock reverb's space (SPRING REV first), which leaves the FX2 menu. It cannot be combined with Analog BD yet.
Author's functional MKII report (7–9 Oct 2026) covers routing, levels, everyday flows, saving and power; no timed stress run or chip timing.

USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB on the Modwerk beta base, which carries Output Matrix’s DSP engine resident and dormant, owns its boot widenings and admits this exact package through a trust row built into it. Its compiled bytes that coincide with stock are copied at install from bytes the base checks against its running stock, so the package carries no stock bytes. It needs that exact base; with an older base the site asks for a base update first. Removing it is refused while MATRIX is selected: switch the AUDIO page back first. Host tests only: the emulator controllers scenario has not run, and there is no hardware run of this package. The owner waived hardware evidence for this exact version’s USB package for the beta.

USB package rebuilt for the fixed beta base (beta test run 1, 14 Oct 2026). Its controller never started before (the base's owned DSP job channel closed at boot), so MATRIX could not be chosen. Fixed; outside MATRIX its frame hook no longer takes the write lease. Seen on a development twin of the fixed base: MATRIX entered, T3 routed to MN and PHN as expected in USB recordings, and left with levels unchanged. Not yet tested: the tester image, mono jacks and a power cycle.

Site sync on the beta base (beta test run 2, 14 Oct 2026; the package is unchanged): removing it while its controller runs no longer ends the sync with “The Octatrack refused this step.” The base answers the first removal busy while it stops the controller and drops the staged package; the site now stages it again, as it does for the base's other busy refusals. Checked on a development twin through the development link (Sidechain installed, running, removed in one command) and by the site's tests; the site's own path has not run on the unit yet.

USB package bound to the new beta base acf91e0a (beta test run 2, 14 Oct 2026, rebuilt 15 Oct with the resident engines placed on demand, BBD Delay's chooser row and a startup without the wave's outline; the base's addresses moved, so the package is relinked against them, its module code unchanged and not yet run on hardware): the base now puts a removed machine's per-track routines back to stock, shows what a picked effect took and each core's DSP budget (the STATUS page's new DSP rows; DSP FULL comes from it), and no longer refuses effect picks for a bank whose Parts never fitted. A tester base from before needs the base update first.
